name: Rokaro's Letter
summary: Rokaro’s Letter carries a request from Shadowprey Village to Myranda the Hag in the Western Plaguelands. Its role in a plan against the Black Dragonflight depends on what the letter does not reveal.

sections.title: A Message to Myranda
sections.body: At Shadowprey Village in Desolace, Rokaro sends you with a message for Myranda the Hag at Sorrow Hill. She is a former master illusionist of Lordaeron, and Rokaro believes her skill with disguise may help fool the Black Dragonflight. He asks you to bring the letter to her, so she can judge whether the cause deserves her aid.

sections.title: What It Carries
sections.body: When Myranda reads Rokaro’s Letter at Sorrow Hill, she finds it intentionally blank. The silence is its safeguard: if the bearer were captured or slain, no written plans could be found. Myranda recognizes Rokaro’s caution and agrees to help, remembering a favor she owes the Warchief.

faq.answer: Rokaro sent the letter from Shadowprey Village in Desolace to Myranda the Hag.

faq.q: Where is the letter meant to go?
faq.answer: The letter is meant for Myranda the Hag at Sorrow Hill in the Western Plaguelands.
Rokaro seeks Myranda’s mastery of illusion and disguise to help fool the Black Dragonflight.
Rokaro’s Letter is intentionally blank, leaving no written plans to expose if its bearer is captured or slain.
The blank letter protects its purpose by carrying no written information that enemies could discover.
Yes. Myranda agrees to help, citing a favor she owes the Warchief.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you carry Rokaro’s appeal to a former Lordaeron illusionist, seeking aid against the Black Dragonflight.
